title: GTA terms have no relevance in law outside the GTA and cannot be cited in proceedings
principle: Subscribers accept that the GTA's terms, including its dispute-resolution arrangements, have no relevance in law to any claim taken outside the GTA (under paras 6.14/6.15) and cannot be cited in legal proceedings. For a non-subscriber such as CCGUK, GTA rates and timescales are therefore a commercial industry benchmark only, not a legal entitlement and not evidence of the basic hire rate.

title: Insurer claiming it was first to offer a replacement vehicle must say so within 5 working days
principle: If the at-fault insurer believes it was first to offer the customer a suitable free replacement vehicle that ought to have been accepted, it must tell the CHO within 5 working days of receiving the New Claim Advice Form / claim notification. Under the GTA an insurer that misses that window loses the right to refuse payment or seek intervention-level rates on that ground. Benchmark only for a non-subscriber: log the date the NCAF was sent and start a 5-WD clock.

title: New Claim Advice Form to the at-fault insurer within 1 working day
principle: The CHO must advise the at-fault driver's insurer of a potential claim within one working day of agreeing services with the customer, using a New Claim Advice Form (Appendix A) or similar. This is the day-one action in the get-paid-faster playbook; its date starts the insurer's 5-WD windows under 3.6 and 4.2.

title: Insurer to confirm handling centre and claim reference within 5 working days
principle: The insurer must respond to the CHO's New Claim Advice Form within 5 working days of receipt, confirming the correct handling centre and, where known, the claim reference number. Sending the payment pack to the wrong handling centre stops the 6.7 payment clock, so chase this reference at day 5.

title: Cash in lieu of repairs: hire stops on receipt of payment
principle: Where the insurer pays cash in lieu of repairs, the hire is treated as ending immediately after the payment is received. A further hire (subject to need) or loss-of-use payment can be claimed under the GTA if the vehicle is then put in for repair within 3 months of receipt of the cash-in-lieu payment, save in exceptional circumstances. Off-hire trigger for the clocks engine.

title: Hire ends no later than 24 hours after repairs are completed
principle: The hire period ends when the customer's vehicle is repaired and ready for collection and, in any event, not later than 24 hours after repairs are completed and the vehicle is ready for its intended use. The 2026 wording added the 'ready for collection' and 'ready for its intended use' qualifiers. Off-hire trigger: repair-complete notification + 24h.

title: Insurer terminating a hire must give at least 1 working day's notice
principle: An insurer wishing to terminate a hire period must give the CHO at least one working day's notice (working days being Monday to Friday excluding bank holidays). Log the notice date/time and channel; the off-hire deadline is the end of the next working day.

title: Repair monitoring: check authorisation within 3 working days, then before hire should end
principle: The CHO must check with the repairer that the repair has been authorised within 3 working days of the vehicle going in, make a further check after the lesser of 5 working days or 3 working days before the hire should have ended, and check again 3 working days before the hire should have ended. These checks are the monitoring diary entries that defend the hire period.

title: Unreasonable repair delay (2+ working days or >20%) must be notified; checks every 5 working days
principle: A delay is 'unreasonable' if it is at least two working days longer than expected or more than 20% over the estimated hire period notified to the CHO. The CHO must notify the at-fault insurer of every unreasonable delay and of any further delays, and where the repair runs past the original period must check with the repairer every 5 working days. Generates the letter.delay_notice_gta_4_10 template trigger.

title: Total loss: off-hire table (hire ends 5 working days after total-loss payment where CHO dealing, vehicle unroadworthy)
principle: Para 4.14 governs total losses. Per the project brief, the current wording contains an off-hire table: where the CHO is dealing and the vehicle is unroadworthy, hire ends 5 working days after the total-loss payment is received; the insurer must tell the CHO as soon as possible the date its total-loss payment was issued, with the CHO reference. Where the customer says the vehicle is unusable/unroadworthy but an engineer says it is usable, hire is paid until the disagreement is resolved. Earlier GTA versions allowed 7 calendar days after receipt of the final payment, so the 5-WD figure must be confirmed against the 2026 text before use.

title: Non-standard risk driver: additional insurance £5.50 per day, capped at £110 per hire (£148.50 for bikes)
principle: For a non-standard risk driver (under 25 or over 70, under 12 months' driving experience, certain occupations, or convictions giving an unspent ban or 7+ points in the last 4 years) the CHO may charge an additional insurance premium of £5.50 per day, capped at £110 for an individual hire claim (cap £148.50 for motorcycle hires). The additional-driver evidence must be on file to claim it.

title: Single clean Payment Pack submitted as soon as full documentation is available
principle: The CHO submits one clean Payment Pack in support of a single payment request to the at-fault insurer as soon as full documentation is available, with all charges, documents and supporting evidence under an agreed covering letter giving payment details. Splitting heads or sending an incomplete pack restarts the 6.7 clock, so validate the pack before dispatch.

title: Insurers settle within one calendar month of dispatch of a clean Payment Pack to the correct handling centre
principle: Insurers settle the CHO's claim within one calendar month from the date a clean Payment Pack is dispatched to the correct handling centre. The clock runs from dispatch, not receipt, but only if the pack is clean and goes to the right centre (hence 4.2). For a non-subscriber this is the industry-benchmark payment period to quote in chasers, not a contractual right.

title: Late payment additions for hires from 16 March 2026: 0% to day 30, 10% days 31-60, 20% from day 61
principle: For hires starting on or after 16 March 2026, failure to settle within the 6.7 period and subsequent one-month periods attracts late-payment additions to the total invoice: nil up to 30 days, 10% between 31 and 60 days, and 20% from day 61 onwards, counted from submission of a clean Payment Pack (as defined in 6.17). Subscriber-only entitlement; CCGUK may cite the figures only as an industry benchmark (see 2.7(j)) and must not present them as a legal right.

citation: GTA Appendix C, Mitigation Questionnaire / Statement of Truth (16 March 2026)
title: Mitigation Questionnaire and Statement of Truth signed by the hirer
principle: Appendix C is the customer's Mitigation Questionnaire/Statement of Truth, a mandatory Payment Pack item. It records whether the at-fault insurer offered a replacement vehicle before the CHO's services were accepted and, if an offer was received, why it was not acceptable; the CHO must advise the customer of the duty to mitigate. For hires from 30 September 2020 the statement reads 'I believe that the facts stated in this mitigation statement are true' with a contempt-of-court warning. CCGUK's form.mitigation_questionnaire mirrors it and is signed through the e-sign flow; every intervention offer logged in the register must be reflected in it.

citation: GTA Technical Committee, How To Join / Applicant Audit (gtacredithire.com)
title: Joining the GTA: applicant audit £1,890 + VAT and a minimum of 40 qualifying files
principle: A CHO applying for GTA subscriber status must complete the current application form and pass an independent Applicant Audit arranged by the GTA Technical Committee. The audit fee is £1,890 plus VAT, payable before the audit date is confirmed, and the applicant must have at least 40 qualifying claims files (progressed beyond Payment Pack or final-invoice stage with all documentation sent to insurers); the auditor samples from the 40 most recent. CCGUK is not a subscriber, so GTA terms are a benchmark only until this is done.

citation: GTA maximum daily rates 2026-27 (new hires 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027)
title: GTA 2026-27 maximum daily rates: scope and status
principle: The GTA Technical Committee publishes maximum daily settlement rates (ex VAT) by vehicle group for new hires from 1 July 2026 to 30 June 2027, following an independent rate review said to draw on about 16 million vehicle-group pricing data points over 12 months, approved on 25 June 2026. Tables exist for cars (S, P, F, M groups), commercial vehicles (CP pick-ups, PV panel vans and others), private hire/taxi and motorcycles (B1-B6), with a downloadable spreadsheet and legacy rates. CHOs may set rates up to the maximum. For a non-subscriber these are a benchmark, not BHR evidence (2.7(j)). See gta-rates.json for the figures captured.
